cap6_start: CAPUT SEXTUM / De hujus mundi fine
cap7_start: mid PHYS 381 CAPUT SEPTIMUM / De resurrectione carnis
titles: CHAPTER SIX. On the end of this world; heavens pass by free omnipotence, not natural cause
Names of the end; this world began and will end; against Didymus on three worlds
Christians confess the end; Porphyry mocks; against Plato, Xenophanes, Aristotle, Averroes on eternity
Fire is proper, not mere metaphor for wrath vs Puccius; Augustine on conflagration; Magius; starry heaven disputed
Augustine's doubt on the heavens; Greeks and Latins before him affirm corruption of the heavens
II. Whether the world perishes as to substance or only qualities is uncertain; commoner opinion: renovation
Juniors who hold substance-perishing; Chassanis; we prefer renovation yet dare not harshly reject
III. The precise time of the conflagration is unknown; always prepare by watching, prayer, repentance
Against mathematicians' great year and the rabbinic six-thousand-year scheme ascribed to Elijah
Rabbi Isaac's four reasons for six millennia; juniors' additions from Genesis 6, Moses, Jericho, Esdras, Apocalypse
IV. Scripture reveals the last day as not far; signs of Christ's approach — Jews' conversion, gospel preaching
Signs in sun, earth, and sea; Jewish fifteen signs; disputed sign of the cross; sign of the Son of Man
V. Since the world and its goods will soon perish, cling not; Christian wisdom dismisses the world — Cap. 6 close
notes: Liber II Cap. 6 densify COMPLETE. Next mid PHYS 381 CAPUT SEPTIMUM / De resurrectione carnis. No Punch X / ship / ai_promote / mixed commit.
